## Role in the pipeline

| | |
|---|---|
| **Thesis section** | 3.4 selection check (Table 5), 3.5 research design (Table 7), 4.1-4.3 results, 4.4 robustness (Table 11) |
| **Input** | `analysis_sample.rds` (file 4) |
| **Output** | `table_main_results.csv`, `table_robustness.csv`, `table7_robustness_overview.csv`, `fig_coefficients_h1.png`, `fig_within_vs_between.png` |
| **Previous file** | `05_descriptives.qmd` |


## Hypotheses and models

| Hypothesis | Model | Test (supported if) |
|---|---|---|
| **H1** industry distance has an inverted U-shaped effect on revenue growth | `m2` | omnibus equality test of the five distance coefficients (basis), joint test, pairwise contrasts |
| **H2** the negative effect of large industry distance is weaker for equity-based than for non-equity alliances | `m4` | (D3_EQ - D4_EQ) - (D3_NE - D4_NE) < 0 |
| *Additional analysis A1* (no hypothesis): related (D0-D3) vs. unrelated (D4) | `m1` | Wald test of RA - UA |
| *Additional analysis A2* (no hypothesis): related-over-unrelated advantage by governance form | `m3` | (RA_EQ - UA_EQ) - (RA_NE - UA_NE) |

The model names are the same as in the earlier version (`m1` to `m4`). H1 is the
former H2, H2 is the former H4; the former H1 and H3 are reported as additional
analyses without a hypothesis.

**Main specification:** annualised revenue growth from t to t+3 on
`log(1 + alliance counts in t-2 to t)`, four controls (size, ROA, leverage, past growth),
firm fixed effects, industry x year and country x year fixed effects, standard
errors clustered by firm. Firm age is not included (collinear with firm and year FE).

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("00_config.R")
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

d <- readRDS(file.path(path, "analysis_sample.rds"))
d[, sic2 := as.factor(sic2)]

c(firm_years = nrow(d), firms = uniqueN(d$gvkey),
  countries = uniqueN(d$country), country_year_cells = uniqueN(paste(d$country, d$fyear)))
```

## Helper functions

```{r}
#| label: helpers
# Does coefficient a differ from coefficient b? (uses the covariance of the two estimates)
diff_test <- function(m, a, b) {
  v   <- vcov(m)
  est <- coef(m)[[a]] - coef(m)[[b]]
  se  <- sqrt(v[a, a] + v[b, b] - 2 * v[a, b])
  c(est = est, se = se, t = est / se, p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)))
}

# Any linear combination of coefficients (used for the H2 and A2 difference-in-differences)
lin_test <- function(m, k, cv) {
  b <- coef(m); V <- vcov(m)
  est <- sum(cv * b[k])
  se  <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(cv) %*% V[k, k] %*% cv))
  c(est = est, se = se, t = est / se, p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)))
}

# Joint significance of the five distance coefficients (H1, fixest Wald test)
joint_p <- function(m, pattern = "^log1p\\(d") {
  wald(m, keep = pattern, print = FALSE)$p
}

# Omnibus test of H1: are the five distance coefficients equal to each other?
# Four restrictions (D0 = D1, D1 = D2, D2 = D3, D3 = D4), chi-square Wald test
omnibus_p <- function(m, pattern = "^log1p\\(d") {
  nm <- grep(pattern, names(coef(m)), value = TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(nm) == 5)
  R <- matrix(0, nrow = 4, ncol = 5)
  for (i in 1:4) { R[i, i] <- 1; R[i, i + 1] <- -1 }
  rb   <- R %*% coef(m)[nm]
  stat <- as.numeric(t(rb) %*% solve(R %*% vcov(m)[nm, nm] %*% t(R)) %*% rb)
  pchisq(stat, df = 4, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

# p-value of A1 (related vs. unrelated) for any model whose first two coefficients are RA and UA
h1_p <- function(m) {
  nm <- names(coef(m))[1:2]
  diff_test(m, nm[1], nm[2])[["p"]]
}

# One-row table from a test result
tidy <- function(label, x) data.table(test = label, est = x[["est"]], se = x[["se"]],
                                      t = x[["t"]], p = x[["p"]])
```

## Specification

All models are built by one function, so that they differ only in the
alliance variables (and in the one design choice that is varied in a robustness check).

```{r}
#| label: spec
controls <- "ln_at_usd + roa_w + leverage_w + growth_l1_w"
fe_main  <- "gvkey + sic2^fyear + country^fyear"

est <- function(rhs, fe = fe_main, y = "growth_f3_w", data = d, ctrl = controls) {
  rhs_all <- if (is.null(ctrl)) rhs else paste(rhs, "+", ctrl)
  feols(as.formula(paste0(y, " ~ ", rhs_all, " | ", fe)),
        data = data, cluster = ~gvkey)
}

# Alliance variables of the four models (window suffix: _3y = t-2 to t)
# rhs_h1 = A1 (m1), rhs_h2 = H1 (m2), rhs_h3 = A2 (m3), rhs_h4 = H2 (m4)
rhs_h1 <- "log1p(n_rel_3y) + log1p(n_unrel_3y)"
rhs_dist <- function(suffix) paste0("log1p(", cats, suffix, ")", collapse = " + ")
rhs_h2 <- rhs_dist("_3y")
rhs_h3 <- paste("log1p(n_rel_eq_3y) + log1p(n_rel_ne_3y)",
                "log1p(n_unrel_eq_3y) + log1p(n_unrel_ne_3y)", sep = " + ")
rhs_h4 <- paste0(c(rbind(paste0("log1p(", cats, "_eq_3y)"),
                         paste0("log1p(", cats, "_ne_3y)"))), collapse = " + ")

# Readable labels for the tables
dict <- c(growth_f3_w                  = "Revenue growth t to t+3",
          growth_f1_w                  = "Revenue growth t to t+1",
          "log1p(n_rel_3y)"            = "Related alliances (D0-D3)",
          "log1p(n_unrel_3y)"          = "Unrelated alliances (D4)",
          "log1p(d0_same4_3y)"         = "D0 same 4-digit",
          "log1p(d1_same3_3y)"         = "D1 same 3-digit",
          "log1p(d2_same2_3y)"         = "D2 same 2-digit",
          "log1p(d3_same_division_3y)" = "D3 same division",
          "log1p(d4_diff_division_3y)" = "D4 different division",
          "log1p(d0_same4)"            = "D0 same 4-digit (year t)",
          "log1p(d1_same3)"            = "D1 same 3-digit (year t)",
          "log1p(d2_same2)"            = "D2 same 2-digit (year t)",
          "log1p(d3_same_division)"    = "D3 same division (year t)",
          "log1p(d4_diff_division)"    = "D4 different division (year t)",
          "log1p(n_rel_eq_3y)"         = "Related, equity-based",
          "log1p(n_rel_ne_3y)"         = "Related, non-equity",
          "log1p(n_unrel_eq_3y)"       = "Unrelated, equity-based",
          "log1p(n_unrel_ne_3y)"       = "Unrelated, non-equity",
          ln_at_usd                    = "Size (ln assets, USD)",
          roa_w                        = "ROA",
          leverage_w                   = "Leverage",
          growth_l1_w                  = "Past growth",
          gvkey                        = "Firm",
          "sic2^fyear"                 = "Industry x Year",
          "country^fyear"              = "Country x Year")
```

## 1. H1: inverted U-shaped effect of industry distance

**H1:** industry distance has an inverted U-shaped effect on a focal firm's subsequent revenue growth.

One coefficient per category imposes no shape, so the data can show any
pattern (a squared distance term would force a symmetric parabola). An
inverted U requires the middle categories D1-D3 to exceed both extremes
D0 and D4.

```{r}
#| label: m2
m2 <- est(rhs_h2)
summary(m2)

nm2 <- function(k, suffix = "_3y") paste0("log1p(", k, suffix, ")")

# (a) joint test, (b) omnibus test (basis for H1), (c) pairwise contrasts
h1_global <- data.table(test = c("Joint significance of D0-D4", "Omnibus: all five equal"),
                        p = c(joint_p(m2), omnibus_p(m2)))
knitr::kable(h1_global, digits = 4)

pr <- CJ(mid = cats[2:4], ext = cats[c(1, 5)], sorted = FALSE)
pairwise <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pr)), function(i) {
  tidy(paste(pr$mid[i], "-", pr$ext[i]), diff_test(m2, nm2(pr$mid[i]), nm2(pr$ext[i])))
}))
knitr::kable(pairwise, digits = 4, caption = "Pairwise contrasts: middle category minus extreme")
```


### How the three tests fit together

The joint test only asks whether distance matters at all; it can be significant
because both extremes are negative, without any systematic variation with
distance. The omnibus test asks whether the five coefficients differ from each
other, which is the actual shape test. The pairwise contrasts are supporting
evidence only: with six comparisons, one or two below 5% are expected by chance.


## 2. H2: governance form moderates the effect of large distance

**H2:** the negative effect of large industry distance on revenue growth is weaker for
equity-based than for non-equity alliances.

An alliance is equity-based if the SDC Joint Venture Flag is true (a new jointly
owned entity was created) or if the Alliance Technique contains Equity Transfer
or Cross Equity Transfer (see file 1, section 1b); all other alliances are
non-equity (`equity_definition` in `00_config.R`). The governance form is defined
at alliance level but the regression is at firm-year level, so the category counts
are split by governance form instead of using an interaction term. This also works
when a firm forms both types in the same year. Model `m4` therefore has ten alliance
coefficients (five distance categories x two governance forms). The penalty of large
distance is the decline from the moderate category D3 to D4; H2 holds if this decline
is smaller for equity-based alliances.

D3 is the moderate category (the intermediate category with the highest
coefficient in the main distance model `m2` of H1; **check this after the re-run**,
the choice is only valid if D3 is still the highest of D1-D3 in `m2`).

```{r}
#| label: m4
m4 <- est(rhs_h4)
summary(m4)

# which intermediate category is highest in the main model?
coef(m2)[nm2(cats[2:4])]

k_h4 <- c("log1p(d3_same_division_eq_3y)", "log1p(d4_diff_division_eq_3y)",
          "log1p(d3_same_division_ne_3y)", "log1p(d4_diff_division_ne_3y)")
h2_tests <- rbind(
  tidy("Decline D3 to D4, equity-based", diff_test(m4, k_h4[1], k_h4[2])),
  tidy("Decline D3 to D4, non-equity",    diff_test(m4, k_h4[3], k_h4[4])),
  tidy("H2: (D3_EQ - D4_EQ) - (D3_NE - D4_NE)", lin_test(m4, k_h4, c(1, -1, -1, 1))))
knitr::kable(h2_tests, digits = 4)

```{r}
#| label: h2-close
# H2, close end: the rise from D0 to D3 should be smaller for equity-based alliances
k_h4_close <- c("log1p(d3_same_division_eq_3y)", "log1p(d0_same4_eq_3y)",
                "log1p(d3_same_division_ne_3y)", "log1p(d0_same4_ne_3y)")
h2_close <- rbind(
  tidy("Rise D0 to D3, equity-based", diff_test(m4, k_h4_close[1], k_h4_close[2])),
  tidy("Rise D0 to D3, non-equity",   diff_test(m4, k_h4_close[3], k_h4_close[4])),
  tidy("H2 close end: (D3_EQ - D0_EQ) - (D3_NE - D0_NE)",
       lin_test(m4, k_h4_close, c(1, -1, -1, 1))))
knitr::kable(h2_close, digits = 4)
```
```


## 3. Additional analyses

### 3.1 B1: related (D0-D3) vs. unrelated (D4)

Previous research mostly distinguishes related from unrelated alliances. This
analysis keeps that comparison next to the five-category model of H1 (no hypothesis).

```{r}
#| label: m1
m1 <- est(rhs_h1)
summary(m1)

# feols drops singleton observations (firms seen in only one year); they have
# no within-firm variation. Number of observations actually used:
c(sample = nrow(d), used = nobs(m1))

knitr::kable(tidy("A1: related - unrelated", diff_test(m1, "log1p(n_rel_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_3y)")),
             digits = 4)
```


### 3.2 B2: related-over-unrelated advantage by governance form

Same logic as H2 (counts split by governance form, equity definition as in section 2),
but with the two relatedness groups instead of the five categories. No hypothesis.

```{r}
#| label: m3
m3 <- est(rhs_h3)
summary(m3)

k_h3 <- c("log1p(n_rel_eq_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_eq_3y)",
          "log1p(n_rel_ne_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_ne_3y)")

h3 <- rbind(
  tidy("Relatedness advantage, equity-based (RA_EQ - UA_EQ)",
       diff_test(m3, "log1p(n_rel_eq_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_eq_3y)")),
  tidy("Relatedness advantage, non-equity (RA_NE - UA_NE)",
       diff_test(m3, "log1p(n_rel_ne_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_ne_3y)")),
  tidy("A2: (RA_EQ - UA_EQ) - (RA_NE - UA_NE)", lin_test(m3, k_h3, c(1, -1, -1, 1))))
knitr::kable(h3, digits = 4)

# Firms with both alliance types over time
firms_both <- d[, .(any_eq = any(n_jv_3y > 0), any_ne = any(n_ca_3y > 0)), by = gvkey]
firms_both[, .(firms = .N,
               with_equity = sum(any_eq), with_non_equity = sum(any_ne),
               both_types = sum(any_eq & any_ne))]
```


### 3.3 Exploratory: equity main effect (not pre-specified)

Average of the two equity coefficients minus the average of the two
non-equity ones in model `m3`. It is supported ex ante by the commitment
logic (Gulati & Singh, 1998; Kogut, 1988; Mowery et al., 1996) but was not
a pre-specified hypothesis, so it is reported as exploratory.



```{r}
#| label: equity-main
eq_main <- rbind(
  tidy("Equity main effect (avg. equity-based - avg. non-equity)", lin_test(m3, k_h3, c(0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5))),
  tidy("Within related: equity-based - non-equity",   diff_test(m3, "log1p(n_rel_eq_3y)",   "log1p(n_rel_ne_3y)")),
  tidy("Within unrelated: equity-based - non-equity", diff_test(m3, "log1p(n_unrel_eq_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_ne_3y)")))
knitr::kable(eq_main, digits = 4)
```


## 4. Robustness checks (numbering as in thesis 3.5.3 and Table 11)

| Check | What is varied | Model |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** | without country x year FE | `m*_r1` |
| **R2** | without industry x year FE | `m2_r2` |
| **R3** | without firm FE | `m*_r3` |
| **R4** | without control variables | `m*_nc` |
| **R6** | one-year growth horizon | `m2_r4` |
| **R7** | alliance window: year t only, 2, 4, 5 years | `m2_r5_*` |
| **R9** | exclude 2009-2015 (SDC coverage gap) | `m*_r6` |
| design | linear counts, any-alliance indicator, cut D2/D3 (all A1), USD 20m floor (H1) | `m1_lin`, `m1_dum`, `m1_c2`, `m2_f20` |
| R19 (not in Table 11) | two-way clustering: firm and year (vs. firm only) | `m2_tw` |
| R20 (not in Table 11) | quadratic-in-distance functional form (vs. five distance categories) | `m2_quad` |

Each check changes one thing relative to the main specification. R8 to R18 are in
a separate file (`07_additional_robustness_checks.qmd`); R19 and R20 are new here.



```{r}
#| label: robustness
# R1-R3: fixed-effect structure
fe_r1 <- "gvkey + sic2^fyear"
fe_r2 <- "gvkey + country^fyear"
fe_r3 <- "sic2^fyear + country^fyear"

m1_r1 <- est(rhs_h1, fe_r1); m2_r1 <- est(rhs_h2, fe_r1); m3_r1 <- est(rhs_h3, fe_r1)
m2_r2 <- est(rhs_h2, fe_r2)
m1_r3 <- est(rhs_h1, fe_r3); m2_r3 <- est(rhs_h2, fe_r3)

# R4: one-year growth horizon (winsorised within the analysis sample)
m2_r4 <- est(rhs_h2, y = "growth_f1_w")

# R5: alliance window
m2_r5_t <- est(rhs_dist(""))      # alliances in year t only
m2_r5_2 <- est(rhs_dist("_w2"))
m2_r5_4 <- est(rhs_dist("_w4"))
m2_r5_5 <- est(rhs_dist("_w5"))

# R6: exclude the SDC coverage gap 2009-2015
d_gap <- d[!(fyear %in% 2009:2015)]
m2_r6 <- est(rhs_h2, data = d_gap)
m3_r6 <- est(rhs_h3, data = d_gap)
m4_r1 <- est(rhs_h4, fe_r1)          # H2 under R1
m4_r3 <- est(rhs_h4, fe_r3)          # H2 under R3 (across firms)
m4_r6 <- est(rhs_h4, data = d_gap)   # H2 under R6

# Design choices
m1_lin <- est("n_rel_3y + n_unrel_3y")                         # linear counts

d[, `:=`(any_rel   = as.integer(n_rel_3y > 0),                 # any-alliance indicator
         any_unrel = as.integer(n_unrel_3y > 0))]
m1_dum <- est("any_rel + any_unrel")

d[, `:=`(n_rel_c2   = d0_same4_3y + d1_same3_3y + d2_same2_3y,   # cut between D2 and D3
         n_unrel_c2 = d3_same_division_3y + d4_diff_division_3y)]
m1_c2 <- est("log1p(n_rel_c2) + log1p(n_unrel_c2)")

m2_f20 <- est(rhs_h2, data = d[revt_usd_lag >= 20])            # USD 20 million revenue floor

# Numbers needed for thesis section 3.3.2
round(diff_test(m1_c2, "log1p(n_rel_c2)", "log1p(n_unrel_c2)"), 4)   # est = X (cut D2/D3)
round(coef(m2_r5_5), 4)                                               # D4 coefficient at 5 years = Y

# R4: without control variables
m1_nc <- est(rhs_h1, ctrl = NULL)
m2_nc <- est(rhs_h2, ctrl = NULL)
m3_nc <- est(rhs_h3, ctrl = NULL)
m4_nc <- est(rhs_h4, ctrl = NULL)

# tests, same as in the main models (A1, H1, A2, H2)
round(diff_test(m1_nc, "log1p(n_rel_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_3y)"), 4)
c(joint_p = joint_p(m2_nc), omnibus_p = omnibus_p(m2_nc))
round(lin_test(m3_nc, k_h3, c(1, -1, -1, 1)), 4)
round(lin_test(m4_nc, k_h4, c(1, -1, -1, 1)), 4)
round(lin_test(m4_nc, k_h4_close, c(1, -1, -1, 1)), 4)

# nine-column check for the table
etable(m2_nc, m2, m4_nc, m4, m1_nc, m1, m3_nc, m3, dict = dict,
       headers = c("H1 no ctrl", "H1", "H2 no ctrl", "H2", "A1 no ctrl", "A1", "A2 no ctrl", "A2"),
       digits = 4, fitstat = ~ n + r2 + wr2)

# direction of the R3 results (across firms)
m1_r3 <- est(rhs_h1, fe = "sic2^fyear + country^fyear")
m3_r3 <- est(rhs_h3, fe = "sic2^fyear + country^fyear")
round(diff_test(m1_r3, "log1p(n_rel_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_3y)"), 4)
round(lin_test(m3_r3, k_h3, c(1, -1, -1, 1)), 4)
round(lin_test(m4_r3, k_h4, c(1, -1, -1, 1)), 4)   # H2 across firms

m2_r3 <- est(rhs_h2, fe = "sic2^fyear + country^fyear")
round(coef(m2_r3)[grep("^log1p\\(d", names(coef(m2_r3)))], 4)
round(diff_test(m2_r3, "log1p(d3_same_division_3y)", "log1p(d0_same4_3y)"), 4)
round(diff_test(m2_r3, "log1p(d3_same_division_3y)", "log1p(d4_diff_division_3y)"), 4)
```

### R19: two-way clustering (firm and year)

Standard errors are clustered by firm throughout. Firm-year observations within
the same year can also be correlated (common macro or industry-wide shocks that
the industry x year and country x year fixed effects do not fully absorb), so
this check clusters two-way by firm and by fiscal year instead.

```{r}
#| label: r19-twoway
m2_tw <- feols(as.formula(paste0("growth_f3_w ~ ", rhs_h2, " + ", controls, " | ", fe_main)),
               data = d, cluster = ~gvkey + fyear)

etable(m2, m2_tw, dict = dict, digits = 4, fitstat = ~ n + r2 + wr2,
       headers = c("Main (cluster: firm)", "R19 (cluster: firm + year)"))
round(c(main_omnibus_p = omnibus_p(m2), tw_omnibus_p = omnibus_p(m2_tw),
        main_joint_p = joint_p(m2), tw_joint_p = joint_p(m2_tw)), 4)
```

### R20: quadratic-in-distance functional form

The main specification (`m2`) imposes no shape on the five distance categories,
so an inverted U is not assumed. This check instead collapses the five categories
into one continuous distance score per firm-year -- the alliance-count-weighted
mean of the category index 0 (D0) to 4 (D4) -- and tests a linear and a squared
term on it. Firm-years with no alliance in the window get a distance of 0,
consistent with how `log1p(N)` already treats "no alliance" as the reference
case. An inverted U-shape implies a positive linear term and a negative squared
term, jointly significant.

```{r}
#| label: r20-quadratic
d[, n_all_3y := d0_same4_3y + d1_same3_3y + d2_same2_3y + d3_same_division_3y + d4_diff_division_3y]
d[, avg_dist := fifelse(n_all_3y == 0, 0,
                        (0 * d0_same4_3y + 1 * d1_same3_3y + 2 * d2_same2_3y +
                           3 * d3_same_division_3y + 4 * d4_diff_division_3y) / n_all_3y)]
d[, avg_dist_sq := avg_dist^2]

m2_quad <- est("avg_dist + avg_dist_sq")
summary(m2_quad)
wald(m2_quad, keep = "avg_dist", print = FALSE)$p   # joint test of avg_dist and avg_dist_sq
```


### Table 7: overview of design choices

Main p = p-value of the main specification; Alt. p = p-value of the alternative.
For the H1 rows the joint test is reported as in the thesis; the omnibus test
(the actual basis for H1) is added in the last two columns. The rows for the
related/unrelated comparison belong to additional analysis A1. H2 is covered
across the same design choices in the overview table below (`table9`).

```{r}
#| label: table7
row7 <- function(group, choice, alternative, stat, m_main, m_alt) {
  if (stat == "Joint test (H1)") {
    data.table(group, choice, alternative, statistic = stat,
               main_p = joint_p(m_main), alt_p = joint_p(m_alt),
               main_omnibus_p = omnibus_p(m_main), alt_omnibus_p = omnibus_p(m_alt))
  } else {
    data.table(group, choice, alternative, statistic = stat,
               main_p = h1_p(m_main), alt_p = h1_p(m_alt),
               main_omnibus_p = NA_real_, alt_omnibus_p = NA_real_)
  }
}
s_h1 <- "Joint test (H1)"; s_a1 <- "RA - UA (A1)"

table7 <- rbindlist(list(
  row7("Model",       "Country x year fixed effects", "R1: without them",           s_h1, m2, m2_r1),
  row7("Model",       "Industry x year fixed effects", "R2: without them",          s_h1, m2, m2_r2),
  row7("Model",       "Firm fixed effects",           "R3: without them",           s_h1, m2, m2_r3),
  row7("Model", "Control variables", "R4: without them", s_h1, m2, m2_nc),
  row7("Measurement", "Growth horizon: three years",  "R6: one-year growth",        s_h1, m2, m2_r4),
  row7("Measurement", "Alliance window: three years", "R7: year t only",            s_h1, m2, m2_r5_t),
  row7("Measurement", "Alliance window: three years", "R7: two years",              s_h1, m2, m2_r5_2),
  row7("Measurement", "Alliance window: three years", "R7: four years",             s_h1, m2, m2_r5_4),
  row7("Measurement", "Alliance window: three years", "R7: five years",             s_h1, m2, m2_r5_5),
  row7("Measurement", "Alliance counts: ln(1 + N)",   "Linear counts",              s_a1, m1, m1_lin),
  row7("Measurement", "Alliance counts: ln(1 + N)",   "Indicator for any alliance", s_a1, m1, m1_dum),
  row7("Measurement", "Relatedness cut: D3 | D4",     "Cut between D2 and D3",      s_a1, m1, m1_c2),
  row7("Sample",      "SDC coverage gap 2009-2015",   "R9: exclude these years",    s_h1, m2, m2_r6),
  row7("Sample",      "Revenue floor: USD 10 million", "USD 20 million",            s_h1, m2, m2_f20)))

knitr::kable(table7, digits = 4)
fwrite(table7, file.path(path, "table7_robustness_overview.csv"))

#| label: robustness-all
# One row per design choice: p-values of the primary test of each hypothesis
# (H1 = omnibus test of m2; H2 = moderation test of m4 at the far end (D3 to D4)
#  and at the close end (D0 to D3); A1 and A2 = additional analyses)
check_p <- function(label, fe = fe_main, y = "growth_f3_w", data = d, ctrl = controls) {
  m1 <- est(rhs_h1, fe, y, data, ctrl)
  m2 <- est(rhs_h2, fe, y, data, ctrl)
  m3 <- est(rhs_h3, fe, y, data, ctrl)
  m4 <- est(rhs_h4, fe, y, data, ctrl)
  data.table(check = label,
             H1_omnibus = omnibus_p(m2),
             H1_joint   = joint_p(m2),
             H2         = lin_test(m4, k_h4,       c(1, -1, -1, 1))[["p"]],
             H2_close   = lin_test(m4, k_h4_close, c(1, -1, -1, 1))[["p"]],
             A1         = diff_test(m1, "log1p(n_rel_3y)", "log1p(n_unrel_3y)")[["p"]],
             A2         = lin_test(m3, k_h3, c(1, -1, -1, 1))[["p"]])
}

res <- rbindlist(list(
  check_p("Main specification"),
  check_p("R1: without country x year FE", fe = "gvkey + sic2^fyear"),
  check_p("R2: without industry x year FE", fe = "gvkey + country^fyear"),
  check_p("R3: without firm FE", fe = "sic2^fyear + country^fyear"),
  check_p("R4: without controls", ctrl = NULL),
  check_p("R6: one-year growth", y = "growth_f1_w"),
  check_p("R9: excluding 2009-2015", data = d[!(fyear %in% 2009:2015)]),
  check_p("USD 20 million floor", data = d[revt_usd_lag >= 20])
))
num <- setdiff(names(res), "check")
res[, (num) := lapply(.SD, round, 4), .SDcols = num]
knitr::kable(res)
fwrite(res, file.path(path, "table9_all_hypotheses.csv"))
```

## 5. Regression tables

```{r}
#| label: tables
ord <- c("D0", "D1", "D2", "D3", "D4", "Related", "Unrelated")

tab_main <- etable(m2_r1, m2, m4, m1_r1, m1, m3, dict = dict,
                   headers = c("H1 (R1)", "H1", "H2", "A1 (R1)", "A1", "A2"),
                   digits = 4, fitstat = ~ n + r2 + wr2, order = ord)
knitr::kable(tab_main)
fwrite(as.data.table(tab_main), file.path(path, "table_main_results.csv"))

tab_rob <- etable(m2, m2_r1, m2_r2, m2_r3, m2_r4, m2_r6, m2_r5_t, m2_f20, dict = dict,
                  headers = c("Main", "R1", "R2", "R3", "R6 (1-yr growth)", "R9 (excl. 2009-15)",
                              "R7 (year t)", "USD 20m floor"),
                  digits = 4, fitstat = ~ n + r2 + wr2)
knitr::kable(tab_rob)
fwrite(as.data.table(tab_rob), file.path(path, "table_robustness.csv"))
```

The relevant R² is the **within** R² (`wr2`), the share of variation explained
after the fixed effects are taken out; `summary()` reports the adjusted R², `etable()`
the plain R².

```{r}
#| label: fig-coef
#| fig-width: 6.3
#| fig-height: 3.8
fam <- "Times New Roman"
show_band <- TRUE   # TRUE = grey area for the moderate categories, FALSE = no area

co <- as.data.table(coeftable(m2), keep.rownames = "term")[grepl("^log1p\\(d", term)]
setnames(co, c("Estimate", "Std. Error"), c("est", "se"))
co[, `:=`(est = 100 * est, se = 100 * se)]            # percentage points
lab <- c("D0\nsame 4-digit", "D1\nsame 3-digit", "D2\nsame major group",
         "D3\nsame division", "D4\ndifferent division")
co[, `:=`(x = 1:5, lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se)]
co[, txt := sub("-", "\u2212", sprintf("%.2f", est))]  # proper minus sign

# smooth inverted-U curve: quadratic fit to the five estimates (illustration only)
fit   <- lm(est ~ x + I(x^2), data = co)
curve <- data.table(x = seq(1, 5, length.out = 100))
curve[, y := predict(fit, newdata = curve)]

p_coef <- ggplot(co, aes(x = x, y = est)) +
  { if (show_band) annotate("rect", xmin = 1.5, xmax = 4.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey92") } +
  { if (show_band) annotate("text", x = 3, y = 1.02, label = "Moderate distance (D1\u2013D3)",
                            family = fam, fontface = "bold", size = 3.9, colour = "black") } +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = curve, aes(x = x, y = y), colour = "grey30",
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.5, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, colour = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(y = hi, label = txt), vjust = -0.6, family = fam, size = 3.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5, labels = lab, expand = expansion(add = 0.45)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-1, 1, 0.5),
                     labels = function(x) sub("-", "\u2212", format(x, nsmall = 1))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1.4, 1.1)) +
  labs(x = "Industry distance between partners",
       y = "Effect on annualised growth (pp)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11, base_family = fam) +
  theme(axis.text    = element_text(colour = "black", size = 10.5),
        axis.title   = element_text(colour = "black", size = 12),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
        axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)),
        axis.line    = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
        axis.ticks   = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4))
p_coef
ggsave(file.path(path, "fig_coefficients_h1.png"), p_coef,
       width = 6.3, height = 3.8, dpi = 300)

```{r}
```{r}
#| label: fig-panels
#| fig-width: 7.5

fam <- "Times New Roman"

get_co <- function(m, spec) {
  x <- as.data.table(coeftable(m), keep.rownames = "term")[grepl("^log1p\\(d", term)]
  setnames(x, c("Estimate", "Std. Error"), c("est", "se"))
  x[, `:=`(est = 100 * est, se = 100 * se, spec = spec, x = 1:5)]      # percentage points
  x[, `:=`(lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se)]
}

m2_r11 <- est(rhs_h2, data = d[country == "USA"])
med_size_for_panels <- median(d$ln_at_usd, na.rm = TRUE)
m2_r12 <- est(rhs_h2, data = d[ln_at_usd <= med_size_for_panels])

lev <- c("(a) Main\nspecification",
         "(b) Without firm\nfixed effects (R3)",
         "(c) Without control\nvariables (R4)",
         "(d) Five-year\nalliance window (R7)",
         "(e) United States\nfirms (R11)",
         "(f) Firms below\nmedian size (R12)")
d <- rbind(get_co(m2,      lev[1]),
           get_co(m2_r3,   lev[2]),
           get_co(m2_nc,   lev[3]),
           get_co(m2_r5_5, lev[4]),
           get_co(m2_r11,  lev[5]),
           get_co(m2_r12,  lev[6]))
d[, spec := factor(spec, levels = lev)]

# main specification as a grey dashed reference line in panels (b) to (d)
ref <- d[spec == lev[1], .(x, est_ref = est)]
dr  <- d[spec != lev[1]][ref, on = "x", nomatch = 0]

p_panels <- ggplot(d, aes(x = x, y = est)) +

### Governance form (H2)

```{r}
#| label: fig-h2
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-height: 3.8
fam   <- "Times New Roman"
dodge <- 0.12   # small horizontal offset so the two series do not overlap

cf <- as.data.table(coeftable(m4), keep.rownames = "term")[
  grepl("^log1p\\(d[0-4]_.*_(eq|ne)_3y\\)$", term)]
setnames(cf, c("Estimate", "Std. Error"), c("est", "se"))
cf[, `:=`(est = 100 * est, se = 100 * se)]                       # percentage points
cf[, gov := factor(ifelse(grepl("_eq_3y", term), "Equity-based", "Non-equity"),
                   levels = c("Equity-based", "Non-equity"))]
cf[, x  := as.integer(sub("^log1p\\(d([0-4]).*$", "\\1", term)) + 1L]
cf[, xp := x + ifelse(gov == "Equity-based", -dodge, dodge)]
cf[, `:=`(lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se)]
stopifnot(nrow(cf) == 10)

lab2 <- c("D0\nsame 4-digit", "D1\nsame 3-digit", "D2\nsame major group",
          "D3\nsame division", "D4\ndifferent division")

p_h2 <- ggplot(cf, aes(x = xp, y = est, group = gov)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 1.5, xmax = 4.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey92") +
  annotate("text", x = 3, y = 1.2, label = "Moderate distance (D1\u2013D3)",

  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, colour = gov), width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = gov, shape = gov), size = 2.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("black", "grey45")) +
  scale_shape_manual(NULL,  values = c(16, 17)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(NULL, values = c("solid", "dashed")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5, labels = lab2, expand = expansion(add = 0.45)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-2, 1, 1),
                     labels = function(x) sub("-", "\u2212", format(x, nsmall = 1))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-2.3, 1.4)) +
  labs(x = "Industry distance between partners",
       y = "Effect on annualised growth (pp)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11, base_family = fam) +
  theme(axis.text    = element_text(colour = "black", size = 10.5),
        axis.title   = element_text(colour = "black", size = 12),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),

        legend.position      = "right",
        legend.direction     = "vertical",
        legend.justification = "center",
        legend.text          = element_text(size = 10.5),
        legend.key.width     = grid::unit(1.2, "cm"),

ggsave(file.path(path, "fig_coefficients_h2.png"), p_h2,

#| label: selection-check
# Table 5 in the thesis: growth history and size by closest alliance distance.
# Computed here rather than in 05_descriptives.qmd because it needs the
# regression-ready sample d built in this file.
# Do firm-years with close partners already differ in growth history and size?
cnt <- paste0(cats, "_3y")
dd  <- copy(d)
dd[, closest := NA_character_]
for (k in rev(seq_along(cats))) dd[get(cnt[k]) > 0, closest := cats[k]]   # the closest category is written last
dd[is.na(closest), closest := "no alliance"]
dd[, closest := factor(closest, levels = c("no alliance", cats))]
sel <- dd[, .(firm_years          = .N,
              past_growth_median  = median(growth_l1_w, na.rm = TRUE),
              past_growth_mean    = mean(growth_l1_w,   na.rm = TRUE),
              size_median         = median(ln_at_usd,   na.rm = TRUE),
              leverage_median     = median(leverage_w,  na.rm = TRUE),
              roa_median          = median(roa_w,       na.rm = TRUE)),
          by = closest][order(closest)]
knitr::kable(sel, digits = 3, caption = "Table 5: Growth history and size by closest alliance distance")
